To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Ca2+‐dependent Ca2+‐transporting enzyme, Ca2+‐adenosine triphosphatase (Ca2+‐ATPage, EC 3.6.1.3), which plays a key role in intracellular Ca2+ homeostasis, is inhibited by the endogenous regu‐calcin in the nuclei of various organs.

regucalcins are a family of proteins that are involved in the regulation of cellular Ca2+ homeostasis and Ca2+ signaling in a variety of cells, and that they may play an important role as a Ca2+ sensor in the regulation of intracellular Ca2+ homeo‐stasis.
regucalcins in the liver and brain have a regulatory role on Ca2+‐dependent enzymes, including Ca2+ sequestering enzymes, and that regucaicn may be a physiological regulator of Ca2+ homeostasis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of endogenous Regucalcin in regulating Ca2+‐sequestrating enzyme (Ca2+‐AT‐Pase) in rat liver nuclei.
the role of endogenous calcium‐binding protein regucalcin, which is a Ca2+‐sequestrating enzyme in rat liver nuclei, in the regulation of nuclear Ca2+ ATPase activity.
the role of endogenous calcium‐binding protein, regucalcin, in the regulation of nuclear calcium‐sequestering enzyme, Ca2+‐activated ATPase, in rat liver.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the endogenous Regucalcin has a suppressive role on nuclear Ca2 +‐ATPase and Ca2 +‐sequestration in the nuclei, which is in contrast to the stimulatory effect of exogenous Regucalcins in the mitochondria and the endoplasmic reticulum.
regucalcins, in general, are Ca2+ binding proteins and Ca2+ binding to regucalcins is essential for the biological activity of regucalcins.
regucalcins are multifunctional proteins that have an inhibitory effect in Ca2+‐dependent signal transduction pathways.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

regucalcins are a new type of protein, which are widely distributed in animal tissues and organs and have a suppressive effect against the activation of Ca2+ signal‐transmitting enzymes, such as Ca2+‐dependent ATPase, Ca2+‐activated ATPase, CaM‐kinase, and Ca2+/calmodulin‐dependent protein kinase, and also against the activation of calmodulin itself.

regucalcins are a family of proteins that have been found in the nuclei of all cells and tissues of vertebrate animals, including humans, and are involved in a variety of biological functions such as calcium homeostasis, cell proliferation, cell differentiation, and apoptosis.

The main takeaway from our work is that
endogenous regucalicin is a negative regulator of Ca2+ ATPase, an enzyme that sequesters calcium.
regucalcins are involved in calcium regulation in the nucleus.
regucalcins are a class of small, secretory peptides that are found in a variety of tissues and are known to play a role in regulating calcium signaling.
